title: Deferred response mode — proto notes
content:
Context / motivation:
- Sometimes caller workflows can tolerate a delayed answer (seconds -> minutes) if it reduces cost or enables batching across noisy request patterns.
- We already do batching + prefix cache; add an explicit customer-facing 'deferred' mode that: queues, batches, and returns a notification/callback when finished (or pollable status).
- Helpful for: background enrichment, non-interactive assistants, nightly report generation, high-throughput low-urgency tasks.

High-level idea:
- API flag: mode=deferred OR header X-Response-Mode: deferred. Request returns 202 + job_id.
- Backend places request in short-lived queue with QoS tier mapping (customer default + per-request override).
- System groups deferred jobs into batch windows (configurable: 100ms/500ms/2s/30s depending on workload and tenant).
- When job completes, we POST to caller-provided webhook OR mark job complete for poll. Optional payload compression & tokenized summary available.

Primary goals:
- Reduce per-token cost by increasing batching and allowing relaxed SLOs.
- Keep integration surface small (webhook + poll + SDK helpers).
- Provide predictable upper bound on completion time per QoS tier.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want to submit 1000 enrichment prompts and get notified when a batch completes so I can update a datastore asynchronously.
  AC: API returns job_id, webhook receives payload with job_id and outputs; job lifecycle visible in Console.
- As a data-platform owner, I want per-tenant throttles for deferred mode to avoid noisy-tenant amplification.
  AC: Tenant-level config in Console, rate limits visible in metrics.
- As an ML ops engineer, I want a canary test that runs deferred batches on a new model variant for 24h before switching traffic.
  AC: canary flag + metrics pipeline draws separate traces for deferred vs sync.

API sketch (proto):
POST /v1/responses?mode=deferred
Body: { input: ..., model: "redwood-4.1", webhook: "https://svc.example/cb", callback_auth: {bearer: "..."}, qos: "low|standard|high", deadline_seconds: 120 }
Response 202: { job_id: "dfr-...", estimated_wait_seconds: 12 }

GET /v1/responses/{job_id}
Response 200: { status: queued|running|complete|failed, result: {...} }

Webhook (POST) payload example:
{ job_id: "dfr-...", tenant_id: "acct_123", status: "complete", completed_at: "2025-03-01T15:03:12Z", outputs: [{ text: "...", tokens: 143 }], metrics: {tokens: 143, model: "redwood-4.1"} }

SDK convenience: client.deferResponse(input, opts).then(handleReceipt) or client.on('deferred:complete', cb).

Operational notes / architecture thoughts:
- Queue: per-region, per-tenant sharded queue to avoid hot-tenant head-of-line blocking.
- Batching window: dynamic windowing (start small. if backlog increases, widen window up to configurable cap) to hit target batch sizes.
- KV/prefix cache: if deferred jobs share prefixes with hot sync requests, need to ensure cache hits are allowed and counting correct.
- Model selection: allow fallback to cheaper quantized variants for low-QoS deferred jobs.
- Persistence: job metadata TTL (default 7 days) in our job-store; payloads optionally stored encrypted if webhook fails.
- Retries: webhook retry policy with exponential backoff + dead-letter queue. Provide UI to re-send payloads.

Cost model & billing implications:
- Bill tokens normally when model is executed. Might offer discounted token rate for queued/deferred tier (structured as committed discount for reserved capacity customers).
- Introduce "deferred compute credit" accounting to attribute batch savings to tenant usage.
- Console: show estimated savings and realized savings per tenant over time.

Fallbacks / graceful degradation:
- If webhook unreachable after N retries, mark job failed and surface to Console + optional fallback to pollable artifact in UI.
- If batch window exceeds SLA cap for tenant's QoS, should escalate: either run smaller sub-batches or switch to higher-priority execution lane.

Metrics to track (initial):
- deferred_jobs_submitted (by tenant, qos)
- avg_wait_seconds, p90_wait_seconds, p99_wait_seconds
- batch_size_distribution (mean, p95)
- tokens_per_deferred_job
- webhook_success_rate / dlq_count
- cost_per_job vs sync-equivalent

Product UX / Console:
- Per-tenant toggle for enabling deferred mode (on by default for dev), QoS default settings, webhook config, DLQ viewer.
- Timeline view of job status + playback of output.
- Savings estimator (visual).

Open questions / risks:
- Security: webhook callback auth patterns and replay protections. Avoid blind open endpoints; support signed headers and short-lived bearer tokens.
- Data retention policy for job payloads (GDPR / privacy).
- How to surface partial outputs for streaming-like use-cases? Might support progressive-webhook chunks, but increases complexity.
- Complexity vs value: adoption might be low if integration overhead is high. Need SDK helpers and templates.

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Phase 0 (spike): infra prototype in staging that supports queue + single-region webhook delivery + basic console listing. Run with internal test clients for 2 weeks. (owner: infra)
- Phase 1 (MVP): public API + SDK helper + Console toggle. Soft-launch to a small set of partner tenants. Add simple savings dashboard. (owner: product)
- Phase 2: routing by QoS across dedicated/dedicated quantized pools, DLQ tooling, retry controls. (owner: runtime + infra)

Timeline (rough):
- Spike: 3 weeks
- MVP dev + docs: 6-8 weeks
- Partner pilots: 4 weeks

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Talk to SRE about per-tenant queue sharding; check current job-store capacity.
- Draft API contract and add to SDK backlog; figure out signing pattern for callbacks.
- Wire up metrics in telemetry board (add dashboard stub).
- Draft simple customer-facing one-pager for sales/solutions (how deferred mode reduces cost).

Potential names for the feature:
- Deferred Responses
- Async Jobs API
- Background Responses
- Response Queueing

Micro UX samples (copy-paste for docs):
- "You can submit requests in Deferred mode when you don't need immediate response. We will batch work and deliver results via webhook or poll. Estimated completion: ~12s (depends on QoS)."

Edge-case examples to test:
- Very small payloads (single token) vs long context usage (large KV caches).
- Mixed workloads (some tenants send 1k deferred + 1k sync concurrently).
- Webhook endpoints that are slow or misbehaving (status 500, 429, timeouts).

Next steps:
- Sync with Maya, Kai and infra lead this week (Tues) to validate feasibility and queue sizing numbers.
- Build spike ticket in JIRA (INF-4827) and link PR template.

-- Diego
(quick brain-dump; will refine into a one-pager and a PRD skeleton once infra feedback arrives)
